summary.one_liner: tmux is a terminal multiplexer that lets many terminals be created, accessed, and controlled from one screen, and detached and reattached while running in the background.
summary.what_it_does: tmux creates multiple terminal sessions inside a single screen and lets you switch between and control them. A session can be detached to keep running in the background and reattached later. The README says it runs on OpenBSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD, Linux, macOS and Solaris. Building requires libevent 2.x, ncurses, a C compiler, make, pkg-config and yacc or bison. Documentation is in the tmux.1 manpage, with an example config file (example_tmux.conf), a wiki and a FAQ. A bash completion file is included. Running with -v or -vv writes server and client log files for debugging.
use_cases: run multiple terminals in one window
keep long-running shell jobs alive after disconnecting
split a single screen into several shells
manage terminal sessions on a remote server
how_to_run: sh autogen.sh (only when building from version control; requires autoconf, automake and pkg-config)
$ nroff -mdoc tmux.1|less (to read the manpage from the source tree)
notable: Sessions can be detached and reattached, so programs keep running in the background
Builds on several Unix-like systems including the BSDs, Linux, macOS and Solaris
Optional utempter support for updating utmp(5) via --enable-utempter
Listed in awesome-python as a companion to tmuxp, a Python tmux session manager
caveats: Requires libevent 2.x and ncurses to build
Building from git needs autoconf, automake and pkg-config
Listed under awesome-python, but this repository is written in C, not Python
